To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the regeneration of the vertebrate visual pigment, rhodopsins, occurs at different rates along the length of the ROS.
the regeneration of the vertebrate visual pigment rhodopsin in rods is not uniform along the rod outer segments.
in toads and frogs the proximal ends and in rats the distal ends of the rod outer segment regenerate rhodopsins faster than do the distal ends and proximal ends respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the topography of rhodoopsin regeneration in the ROS of vertebrates and with the factors that influence it.
the intracellular topography of the bleaching and the regeneration of the visual pigment of vertebrate rods, and the factors that determine this topography.
understanding the mechanisms of rhodopsins regeneration in vertebrates and with determining the extent to which this process is regulated by light and by retinal pigment epithelial melanin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regeneration of rhodopsins in vertebrate rods is not uniform along the length of the ROS.
the proximal-to-distal gradient of regeneration rates seen in the toad, frog and rat is not due to a gradient in the availability of the retinoids, nor to a gradient of the retinal pigment.
the proximal-distal pattern of regeneration of rhodopsins is a general property of vertebrate rods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regeneration patterns in vertebrates are not a consequence of the way in which the retinoid is stored but rather of the way in it is transported.
the regeneration patterns are not due to the bleaching pattern but to the regeneration pattern.
the regeneration of rhodopsins in the ROS is a highly organized process, and that the organization depends in some way on the morphology of the epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topography of rhodoopsin regeneration in the vertebrate rod is complex and that the retinal pigment epthelium may play an important part in the process.
rhodopsin is not regenerated uniformly along the ROS and the pattern is different in different vertebrate species.
the topography of rhodsopsin regeneration is not a simple function of the location of the pigment in the ROS.
